sheet-1-1.description: Main part of Sheet 1, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the street grid turned so that Nottingham Way runs down the page, covering the centre of the village of Hamilton Square and the district on its west side. In the upper part of the sheet Nottingham Way is the main street; the commercial blocks around the junction with Hamilton Square White Horse Avenue and Yardville Avenue are drawn in detail with brick buildings in pink and frame buildings in yellow, and a radial street pattern is lettered Hamilton Square around the central circle. Along the left side are blocks of dwellings with their lot numbers and house numbers. Lower on the sheet, Nottingham Way E. continues south-east past an office building and a pink brick works building marked at the compass rose, and Yardville Av. runs off to the lower left with scattered dwellings. Block numbers 85 to 90 and 74 are printed. The key to the colours, a compass rose and a water-supply and fire-department note are placed in the margins; the upper right of the sheet carries the Sanborn Map Company cartouche, the street index and an inset locator map of New Jersey, none of which belongs to this part. A heavy line along the right separates this part from a second part, the inset at lower right. The Hamilton Square July 1927 title and the Princeton Map Division stamp are in the margins.
notes: Hamilton Square White Horse Av. is now Whitehorse-Hamilton Square Road and Yardville Av. is now Yardville-Hamilton Square Road.
The street index printed on the sheet lies outside this part's mask.

Map, 50 ft. Title, key map (1200 ft, not placed), index, water/fire notes in the upper right (outside both masks). Part 1: Nottingham Way at Hamilton Square White Horse Av. and Yardville Av. Part 2 (inset, own rotation): Mercer St. east of sheet 2 to Cubberly (not open), Mercer Rubber Co.

sheet-1-2.description: Second part of Sheet 1, the lower right area set off from the main part by a heavy dividing line. It shows the district around Mercer Street and the works of the Mercer Rubber Co. on the east side of Nottingham Way, with Cubberly Avenue running down the right margin. The Mercer Rubber Co. plant occupies the lower right as a large complex of brick buildings drawn in pink, with a smaller part in yellow, a lettered milling building, a stock and storage rooms, a water tank, a watchman's clock and a sprinkler note; a circular tank is shown at the right. North of the works, Mercer Street crosses the part with blocks of frame dwellings and a few outbuildings drawn in yellow, and the lot lines of numbered blocks 71 and 74 are printed. The areas near the top and bottom of the part are marked No Exposure. A north arrow points to the upper right and the scale bar is at the bottom. Large areas at the lower left are blank paper between the works and Nottingham Way.
notes: Mercer is lettered without a suffix; the present street is Mercer Street.
The Mercer Rubber Co. is lettered below the works at the bottom of the part.
Cubberly (lettered "not open") is now Cubberly Avenue.

Map, 50 ft. Title, key map (1200 ft, not placed), index, water/fire notes in the upper right (outside both masks). Part 1: Nottingham Way at Hamilton Square White Horse Av. and Yardville Av. Part 2 (inset, own rotation): Mercer St. east of sheet 2 to Cubberly (not open), Mercer Rubber Co.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, shows the south-eastern side of Hamilton Square along Nottingham Way and Nottingham Way E., with the west end of Maple Shade Av. Park Av. runs across the top. Along the west side of Nottingham Way is a row of buildings, including the Hamilton Square M. E. Church, a hall and a bank, drawn in pink where they are brick, and below them a cluster of shops and dwellings at the corner of Nottingham Way E. and Mercer. On the right the Hamilton Square Public School stands in the upper right as a large pink building. Maple Shade Av. runs diagonally down the right centre, with long narrow lots of small yellow frame dwellings on both sides, numbered blocks 70, 71 and 74 and a compass rose at the centre top. At the lower left Nottingham Way E. runs south-east beside a cemetery and past the Hamilton Square Baptist Church, a large pink building at the lower left corner. Streets are shown with 50 foot widths and water pipes as dashed lines. Parts of the sheet's right margin and the lower edge are vacant fields. A cartouche, the Princeton Map Division stamp and the scale bar are in the margins.
notes: Maple Shade Av. is now Maple Shade Avenue; Park Av. is now Park Avenue; Mercer is now Mercer Street.
The sheet shows the Hamilton Square M. E. Church, Public School and Baptist Church by name.
Hamilton Square White Horse Av. is now Whitehorse-Hamilton Square Road; Yardville Av. is now Yardville-Hamilton Square Road.
Map, 50 ft. Hamilton Square centre: Nottingham Way, Park Av., Maple Shade Av., Mercer, Nottingham Way E.; public school, M.E. and Baptist churches.

sheet-3-1.description: Main part of Sheet 3, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the right of the page, covering the area south and west of the centre of Hamilton Square. Nottingham Way runs down the left side of the page from the top to Park Av. at the bottom, with Sharps Av. branching off to the upper right, Herbert Av. crossing to the lower left with Collins nearby, and a cemetery lettered at the lower left. Park Av. runs across the foot of the sheet and Maple Shade Av. at the lower right. Buildings are chiefly small yellow frame dwellings along Nottingham Way and the nearby streets, with a pink church building south of Herbert Av. Blocks 68, 69, 87, 88 and 92 are numbered and large areas, especially at the left, are open land. A compass rose is at the top and a heavy line on the right separates this part from the second part, which holds Nottingham Way, Burtis Av. and Crest Av. in the upper right. The Hamilton Square July 1927 cartouche, a Princeton Map Division stamp and the scale bar are in the margins.
notes: Sharps Av. is now Paxson Avenue.
Herbert Av. is now Herbert Avenue and Park Av. is now Park Avenue.
Collins (no suffix printed) is a short street off Herbert Av.; today Collins Road, which no longer meets Herbert Avenue in OpenStreetMap.

Map, 100 ft, two parts split by a heavy line. Part 1: Nottingham Way north from Park Av. to beyond Sharps Av. (now Paxson Avenue), Herbert Av., Park Av. to Maple Shade Av. Part 2: Nottingham Way E. south of the Baptist church, Burtis Av., Crest Av.

sheet-3-2.description: Second part of Sheet 3, the upper right of the page set off by a heavy line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the right. It shows Nottingham Way running down the right side from the top of the sheet to Crest Av., and a triangular block between the heavy line and Nottingham Way East bounded by Burtis Av. along the top and Crest Av. at the bottom. Dwellings and outbuildings in yellow front Nottingham Way East, and a few pink buildings, including a church, stand near the top right. A diagonal Burtis Av. runs down the left of the block toward Crest Av. Blocks 90, 74 and 92 are numbered. The area inside the dividing line at the top is blank, with a compass rose at the top of the sheet, and the part is cut off by the heavy line at left and below. The sheet number 3, the cartouche and the Princeton Map Division stamp lie in the margins.
notes: Burtis Av. is lettered twice, along the top and on the diagonal; the modern street is South Burtis Avenue.
Nottingham Way E. is now part of Nottingham Way.

Map, 100 ft, two parts split by a heavy line. Part 1: Nottingham Way north from Park Av. to beyond Sharps Av. (now Paxson Avenue), Herbert Av., Park Av. to Maple Shade Av. Part 2: Nottingham Way E. south of the Baptist church, Burtis Av., Crest Av.

sheet-4-1.description: Main part of Sheet 4, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the right of the page, covering the built-up edge of Mercerville along Nottingham Way. Nottingham Way runs down the page as the main street, crossed from the west by Weston Avenue, Birtin Avenue, Floral Avenue, Highland Avenue and Evergreen, with Washington at the top left and Hamilton Av. running down the left margin. East of Nottingham Way the sheet shows a fan of long narrow lots between diagonal streets: Wilson, Marshall and Mc Adoo, with Daniels and Burleson crossing them, and Lansing Av. and a Weston (marked not open) at the top. Blocks are numbered 33 to 99 and lot numbers run along the streets. Almost all buildings are small yellow frame dwellings with outbuildings, with a few pink (brick or tile) and blue buildings near the top of Nottingham Way, including one labelled as a public service property. Large areas east of Nottingham Way are shown as long unbuilt strips. A diagonal band marked Electric Ry. Right of Way crosses the upper centre and runs again near the lower edge, and a heavy dark line with a compass rose divides this part from a second part at the lower right, whose lots are drawn in the same style. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are shown dashed along several streets. Vacant fields are lettered along the heavy line and in the lower centre, and the scale bar sits at the bottom edge.
notes: Hamilton Av. is now Lenhardt Avenue; the modern Hamilton Avenue is a different street further west.
Highland Av. appears to be the present Lander Drive (placed by position along Nottingham Way; medium confidence).
Marshall is now Marshall Avenue East and Mc Adoo is McAdoo Avenue.
The Electric Ry. Right of Way is now New Jersey Highway 33.
Weston at the top is lettered 'not open' (Weston Avenue to the west is the open street).

Map, 100 ft, Mercerville east. Part 1: Nottingham Way with Washington, Weston, Birtin, Floral, Highland (now Lander Drive), Evergreen, Hamilton Av. (now Lenhardt Avenue), Daniels, Wilson, Marshall, McAdoo, Burleson, Lansing. Part 2 (lower right, behind heavy lines): Nottingham Way and Labaw Av. between Mercerville and sheet 3; not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Nottingham Way at Labaw Av., between Mercerville and sheet 3 (lower right, behind heavy lines) (no street junction in the modern data (Labaw Av. gone); Nottingham Way only; needs step 6b: points carried from sheet-3-1 (Nottingham Way north of Sharps Av.) or parcel corners).

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the right of the page, covers the centre of Mercerville where Nottingham Way, Mercerville White Horse Rd., Princeton Rd. and Edinburg Rd. meet. Mercerville White Horse Rd. runs across the page from the left margin to Princeton Rd. at the right. Nottingham Way enters from the top and divides at the main junction into a branch running to the lower left and Edinburg Rd. running to the lower right. Along Regina near the top right stand the Mercerville Public School (a pink building) and a row of small lots. Further down, Steiner Av. runs between blocks of dwellings, and at the lower left Berkley, Hamilton Av., Mercer and Washington St. serve a set of small lots bounded by the diagonal Electric Railway Right of Way. At the upper left the blocks along Clifford Av., Fenwood Av., Osage Av. and Lowell Av. are mostly open lots with scattered dwellings. Buildings are chiefly yellow frame dwellings with outbuildings, with several pink brick buildings and a few blue ones near the main junction. Block numbers 22 to 47 are printed, and large areas are drawn as unbuilt strips with no buildings. A compass rose, the Hamilton Square July 1927 cartouche with the name Mercerville, a Princeton Map Division stamp and the scale bar appear in the margins.
notes: Hamilton Av. is now Lenhardt Avenue, Mercer is now Getz Avenue, Berkley is now Berkeley Street and Princeton Rd. is now Quakerbridge Road.
Mercerville White Horse Rd. is now White Horse-Mercerville Road; Steiner Av. is Steiner Avenue and Edinburg Rd. is Edinburg Road.
The Electric Railway Right of Way is now New Jersey Highway 33.
Fenwood Avenue is realigned at its south end in the modern street network.

Map, 100 ft, Mercerville centre; north to the right. Nottingham Way, Mercerville White Horse Rd., Princeton Rd. (now Quakerbridge Road), Edinburg Rd., Regina, Steiner, Clifford, Fenwood, Lowell, Osage, Berkley, Hamilton Av. (now Lenhardt), Mercer (now Getz Avenue).

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the right of the page, shows the north-western part of Mercerville on both sides of Nottingham Way, which runs diagonally down the page from the upper centre to the lower right. The sheet is cut along its upper edge by the legend See Map of Trenton, Volume Two; the area above Concord Av. is mostly blank and the strip at the very top is lettered No Exposure. West of Nottingham Way the sheet is laid out in blocks between Grayson, Crescent Av., Winslow Av. and Clifford Av. crossed by Fenwood Av., Lowell Av. and Eaton Av., with block numbers 27 to 79 and long narrow lots numbered along each street. East of Nottingham Way, Concord Av. and Hilhurst Av. run toward the right margin with narrow lots, and a fan of diagonal streets (Vincent Av., Stacy Av., Sheridan Av. and Stratford Av.) crosses the right centre, bounded below by an Electric Ry. Right of Way. Almost all buildings are small yellow frame dwellings with outbuildings, with a few pink and blue buildings along Nottingham Way and a church-like building near the lower centre. Dashed 4 and 6 inch water pipes run in many streets. A compass rose, the Hamilton Square July 1927 cartouche with the name Mercerville, the Princeton Map Division stamp and the scale bar appear in the margins.
notes: Hilhurst Av. is now Hillhurst Avenue and Sheridan Av. is now Sheridan Road.
The Electric Ry. Right of Way is now New Jersey Highway 33.
The strip along the top is marked See Map of Trenton, Volume Two (another volume).
Modern Clifford Avenue sits about 5 to 7 m off its 1927 line and was left out of the georeferencing.

Map, 100 ft, Mercerville north-west; north to the right. Grayson, Concord, Crescent, Hilhurst, Vincent, Winslow, Clifford, Lowell, Fenwood, Eaton, Stacy, Sheridan, Stratford, Nottingham Way. 'See Map of Trenton, Volume Two' strip at the top.
